1.inputFormat: One case. The first token is integer n, the number of array elements. The next n whitespace-separated tokens are signed integers a[0] through a[n-1]. Tokens may be separated by spaces or newlines; there is no additional input.
1.outputFormat: For each element, in original array order, print one line exactly as `index -> value`, using zero-based indices from 0 through n-1. Print no other text.
1.constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000; -1000000000 <= a[i] <= 1000000000 for every i. The array is nonempty. Each input contains exactly one case. Output order is the original left-to-right array order, and indices are zero-based as in the question's example and pseudocode.

62.inputFormat: The first line contains n, the number of elements. The second line contains n space-separated integers. The third line contains the non-negative difference k.
62.outputFormat: Print the number of unordered index pairs (i, j) with i < j for which |a[i] - a[j]| = k. Count each pair of positions once, including duplicate values at different positions. For k = 0, count pairs of equal values at different positions; do not pair an element with itself.
